keyVerseText: Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
rootMeaning: The name Παῦλος (Paûlos) is of Latin origin, reflecting a Roman heritage rather than a Greek root. While it is remotely connected to the Greek verb παύω, meaning 'to stop,' this connection is not direct or primary. The literal sense of the name, derived from Paulus, suggests 'small' or 'little,' which adds a dimension of humility or insignificance beyond the common English gloss simply as 'Paul.' This background enriches the understanding of the name as more than a label, hinting at the Apostle's transformation from modest beginnings to a major figure in Christian history.
usageInScripture: The word Παῦλος appears 163 times in the New Testament, predominantly translated as 'Paul' in 134 instances, indicating its primary function as a proper name. Other translations such as 'when Paul,' 'of Paul,' and 'Paul's' reflect its grammatical usage in various contexts, showing possession or temporal reference. The consistency in translation underscores the central role of the Apostle Paul in the New Testament narrative and highlights the personal identity behind the missionary and theological work recorded in Scripture.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Παῦλος as a name of Latin origin tied to a humble meaning underscores the transformative power of God's grace in the life of the Apostle Paul. Despite the name's modest connotations, Paul became a pivotal instrument in spreading the gospel, demonstrating that God often chooses the seemingly insignificant to accomplish His purposes. This reminds believers that faithfulness and divine calling transcend human status or origin. The frequent mention of Παῦλος in Scripture emphasizes the importance of personal testimony and apostolic authority in the early church, anchoring Christian doctrine and mission in the life of this chosen servant.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 13:7 introduces Sergius Paulus, 'a prudent man,' who summons Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God. The use of 'Saul' here, who is later more commonly referred to as Παῦλος, highlights the transitional identity of the Apostle. The name Παῦλος in this context points forward to the Apostle's future ministry and significance, marking the beginning of his public engagement in spreading the gospel. This verse sets the stage for the profound impact Paul will have as a messenger of God's truth.
